judgments.reasoning_cat1: Splits cash discounts between Owner and Contractor on two enumerated conditions, then sweeps 'Trade discounts, rebates, refunds and amounts received from sales of surplus materials and equipment' to the Owner and requires the Contractor to 'make provisions so that they can be secured'. The list is specific but the closing duty to 'make provisions' has no ascertainable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 9.1.1 [New], which forbids the Contractor from obtaining discounts for its own benefit without seven days' notice and an Owner opportunity to fund them, and against 7.4.2 (proceeds of unused excess materials credited to the Owner); the Addendum materially narrows the 'otherwise ... accrue to the Contractor' half of this clause. Real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Amounts that accrue to the Owner in accordance with Paragraph 9.1 shall be credited to the Owner as a deduction from the Cost of the Work.' A single definite accounting instruction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.1, 7.4.2 and 5.1.1 (Contract Sum is Cost of the Work plus Fee); crediting against the Cost of the Work is consistent throughout. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on what the Contractor 'does not customarily perform with the Contractor's own personnel' and preserves a right not to contract with anyone to whom it has 'reasonable objection' — both are nameable open standards, and 'customarily' governs the whole allocation of self-performed work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 6.5 [New], which prescribes a different procurement route (Preliminary Budget, at least two bids, suppliers 'named by Owner or Architect and reasonably acceptable to Contractor', Change Orders adjusting the Contract Sum) from this clause's 'the Owner shall then determine ... which bids will be accepted'. Two bidding regimes for the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-element test — recommended, qualified, and a conforming bid 'without reservations or exceptions' — followed by a precise difference-based adjustment. Definite as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price this clause adjusts is stated as 'N/A', and against First Addendum 6.5 [New], which routes bid-based adjustments to the Contract Sum instead; the remedy operates on a figure that does not exist. Serious relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States the default one-calendar-month period and then trails off into 'or as follows:' with nothing following, so the alternative invited by the form was never supplied. The default still reads sensibly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.3, whose application and payment days are illegible or unfilled, and 12.1.6 (percentage of completion 'as of the end of the period covered'); the period is the one payment variable that is fixed. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three operative numbers — the day of the month by which the Application must be received, the day of the following month for payment, and the fallback number of days — are all garbled or unreadable here, so the payment timetable cannot be applied from the text. That incompleteness is a mechanical defect that changes what the provision requires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.6.1 (payment 'within the time provided in the Contract Documents') and 14.1.1.3/9.7.1 (stop-work and termination rights keyed to 'the time stated in the Contract Documents'), and First Addendum 12.2.2, which fixes only final payment; several remedies depend on a date this clause fails to fix. Real gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists payrolls, petty cash accounts and receipted invoices and then adds 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect' — an unqualified catch-all after enumerated specifics — followed by a three-term arithmetic test whose components must be read carefully.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.4 [New], which adds subcontractor statements and lien waivers 'all in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' but qualifies its residual item with 'reasonably may require'; the two catch-alls carry different standards for the same submission. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the schedule of values to allocate 'the entire Guaranteed Maximum Price' among portions of the Work, with the Fee shown separately, in such form 'as the Architect may require'. Clear as a mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A', and First Addendum 6.5 [New], which substitutes a Preliminary Budget with an Itemized Schedule of Values representing the 'current best estimate of the Contract Sum'; the sum this schedule must allocate does not exist. Serious incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lesser-of test between actual completion and an expense-to-allocated-share ratio, including expense 'for which the Contractor has made or intends to make actual payment'. The arithmetic is stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 ('N/A' Guaranteed Maximum Price) and 12.1.5; limb (2) divides by 'the share of the Guaranteed Maximum Price allocated to that portion of the Work', which cannot be computed on this contract. Real defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in — 'the amount of each progress payment shall be computed' — whose closing 'as follows:' is lost in the marginal text here; it carries no independent obligation. Minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the six clauses it introduces (12.1.7.1-.6) and 12.1.5; the computation it opens rests on the Guaranteed Maximum Price stated as 'N/A' in 5.2.1. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of the Guaranteed Maximum Price properly allocable to completed Work' — 'properly allocable' is the soft term, but the multiplication it prescribes is otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A', and 12.1.5/12.1.6, which build the same computation on the same missing figure; the first and largest component of every progress payment has no defined base. Serious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds the portion of the Guaranteed Maximum Price allocable to materials stored at the site, or off site 'if approved in advance by the Owner' at 'a location agreed upon in writing'. Conditions are explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 7.5.6 (off-site storage 'at a mutually acceptable location, if approved in advance by the Owner'), A201 9.3.2 (procedures 'satisfactory to the Owner' to establish title) and 5.2.1's 'N/A' Guaranteed Maximum Price; three formulations of the same off-site storage condition plus a missing base figure. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retainage figure is entered as 'N/A percent (N/A %)', which on its face means no retainage is held on the Fee; entering 'N/A' into a percentage blank leaves it arguable whether the parties meant zero or meant to say nothing at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.7.3 [Revision], which restates the identical clause with 'five percent (5%)' retainage, and against Article 1 of the Agreement, which provides that where another Contract Document is inconsistent with the Agreement 'this Agreement shall govern' — the amendment and the priority clause point opposite ways on the same number. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subtract the aggregate of previous payments made by the Owner.' Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.7.1-.3 and 13.2.3, which use the identical subtraction; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subtracts a shortfall 'indicated by the Contractor' in the 12.1.4 documentation 'or resulting from errors subsequently discovered by the Owner's accountants' — the second limb is open-ended in time and has no verification or dispute mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.4 and First Addendum 12.1.4 [New] (which enlarges the required documentation) and 12.1.9/Article 11 (Owner's accountants acting 'in the sole interest of the Owner'); the deduction depends on documents whose content is set by two different provisions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subtracts amounts for which the Architect 'has withheld or nullified a Certificate for Payment as provided in Paragraph 9.5' of A201. A pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.5.1-9.5.3 and Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1 (Owner concurrence required wherever the Architect acts); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is numbered '12.1.9' although the following paragraph carries the same number, so the subcontractor retainage rule and the Architect's-reliance rule share an identifier; it also ends in an agreement to agree on a 'mutually acceptable procedure'. Both the misnumbering and the open procedure are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.7.3 ('N/A' retainage on the Fee), First Addendum 12.1.7.3 (5%) and A201 9.6.2 (pay-through 'reflecting percentages actually retained'); the retainage figures across the documents do not line up, and the duplicate numbering makes cross-references to 12.1.9 ambiguous. Real difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully hedged statement that the Architect may rely on the Contractor's information and is not deemed to have audited it, with verification reserved to the Owner's accountants 'acting in the sole interest of the Owner'. Definite, though it shares its paragraph number with the preceding provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.4.2 (the same disclaimers) and Article 11 (accounting records and audit rights); consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Final payment, constituting the entire unpaid balance of the Contract Sum, shall be made ... when:' — a two-condition gateway, definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.2.1 [New], which adds a third condition (a duly published and recorded Notice of Completion), Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 (no final Certificate until all warranties are received and accepted by the Owner), and 5.1.1/5.2.1, where no Contract Sum figure is stated; the conditions are spread across three documents and the 'unpaid balance' has no fixed referent. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires full performance except the correction obligation 'and to satisfy other requirements, if any, which extend beyond final payment' — an unspecified residual category attached to a completion condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 14.6 [New] (warranties that expressly 'survive ... the final completion of the Work') and A201 12.2.2/9.10.4; the surviving requirements exist but are enumerated elsewhere. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A final Certificate for Payment has been issued by the Architect.' A single objective event.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 (the final Certificate 'will not be issued ... until all warranties and guarantees have been received and accepted by the Owner') and 12.2.3; issuance is conditioned elsewhere but not inconsistently. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes final payment at 'no later than 30 days after the issuance of the Architect's final Certificate for Payment, or as follows:' and then leaves the alternative blank, so the form invites a substitute that never appears in this document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.2.2 [Revision], which sets final payment at fifty days after recordation of the Notice of Completion or five business days after a lien-free title endorsement, whichever is earlier, and against Article 1 ('If anything in the other Contract Documents is inconsistent with this Agreement, this Agreement shall govern'); two irreconcilable final-payment deadlines with a priority clause favouring the older one. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sequenced 30-day/seven-day review procedure ending with an express statement that its time periods 'supersede those stated in Subparagraph 9.4.1' of A201. Definite and self-aware.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.4.1 (which it expressly displaces), 12.2.1/First Addendum 12.2.1 [New], Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1 and First Addendum 12.2.2 [Revision]; the final-payment gateway is described in four documents with different triggers and clocks. Real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Gives a 30-day window to demand arbitration and then, in the same sentence, describes it as 'this 10-day period', so the forfeiture deadline is stated twice with two different numbers; a mismatch of that kind in a provision that makes an amount 'binding on the Contractor' is exactly the sort of mechanical error that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.5/4.6 (mediation as a condition precedent to arbitration and the demand-timing rules) and 12.2.3; this clause lets the Contractor go straight to arbitration 'without a further decision of the Architect', which cuts across the A201 claims machinery. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimburses post-final-payment correction costs 'but not in excess of the Guaranteed Maximum Price' and requires savings to be recalculated 'as provided in Paragraph 5.2', a cross-reference that is garbled here. Both the cap and the reference are doubtful on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A' and the savings-participation insert was left blank, and against A201 12.2.2/12.2.5; the clause conditions payment on a cap and a savings arrangement that this contract never created. Serious relational defect.
